pairings.sermonLocator: No. 126, Justification by Grace; PDF p. 4, division II, definition of justification; opening text Romans 3:24 on p. 1
pairings.connection: Hodge's distinction between justification and inward sanctification can be read beside Spurgeon's courtroom explanation of justification. Both selected passages describe a forensic act and distinguish it from mere pardon; Spurgeon's illustration makes the distinction accessible in preaching.
pairings.limit: Related doctrinal argument, not an identical proof-text claim: the inspected Hodge paragraph cites Romans 4:5, while the sermon opens with Romans 3:24. The analogy's every detail and the whole sermon have not been independently reviewed.

pairings.sermonLocator: No. 310, Christ Our Substitute; PDF pp. 2-3, transition to the three-part argument and the sinlessness of the substitute; main text on p. 1
pairings.connection: Both address 2 Corinthians 5:21 and distinguish Christ's personal sinlessness from his representative bearing of his people's sin. Owen offers extended exegesis; Spurgeon develops the qualification of a sinless substitute for a congregation.
pairings.limit: Selected doctrinal paragraphs only. Spurgeon's opening penal-policy analogy and polemical characterizations are historical context, not a project policy position or a verified account of his opponents.
